svg.title: A scheduling model must preserve both values and progress
svg.desc: No kernel, observed SM assignment or hardware timing is claimed by these reference sketches
svg.text: A scheduling model must preserve both values and progress
No kernel, observed SM assignment or hardware timing is claimed by these reference sketches
Resident → eligible → selected for instruction issue
A resident warp may wait for data or synchronization while other work progresses.
Resident warps, active lanes and useful output are different measurement populations.
Divergence: same item tags, different descriptor order
64 items, two warps, L = 8 abstract path positions: interleaved 32; grouped 16.
Both have 512 useful lane-instruction positions; grouping/scattering costs are additional.
Ordinary blocks own independent output regions
Seven ten-thread blocks cover 70 elements under all 7! = 5,040 serial orders.
Block IDs do not prescribe start order or SM placement; replay is not a concurrency proof.
Resident blocks waiting on an unstarted predecessor can prevent progress.
A block barrier or fence is not a grid rendezvous; use a supported dependency contract.
Next authoring: M3-C05 memory hierarchy. Reading successor M3-C04 awaits memory/resource prerequisites.
